answer: A newcomer earns standing by forging a mooring chain at a harbour haven, logging each link — heat, hammer count, and a voyage log of the chain's first sea trial, witnessed by a neighbour. Two harbour smiths verify the log within six days, checking heat against the forge record and the voyage log against the tide table. A copied log, a link the forge never heated, or a missing trial voids the season, burns the 55-credit stake and bars the sponsor a year. One honest season costs 55 credits; a thousand fakes need 1,000 stakes and 1,000 seasons of forged chains, each checked at the forge.
